A1.justification: Both PDFs contain readable DYNMoE methods, empirical results, figures, tables and Appendices A-C. Corresponding material can be matched reliably despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original DYNMoE experiments on DomainBed, GLUE and vision-language benchmarks, including auxiliary-loss and inference-routing ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds resource measurements, learning-rate-specific results, convergence curves and routing diagnostics.

M1.justification: Equations (1)-(8) and Algorithm 1 retain the same gating, gradient approximation, expert averaging, inference fallback, auxiliary loss and expert addition/removal rules. Added explanations and conflicting scheduling statements do not establish an algorithmic redesign.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four DomainBed datasets, five GLUE tasks and ten vision-language benchmarks. Added resource, learning-rate and routing analyses introduce no new dataset, domain or task scenario.

E2.justification: The GMoE baselines, fixed-(K,k) MoE configurations, GShard-loss variant, MoE-LLaVA and dense vision-language comparators are retained. New efficiency tests reuse MoE-LLaVA. Figure 1(b)'s comparators already appeared in v1 Figure 7.

E3.justification: v2 adds controlled efficiency evaluation using one 80-GB A100, 16 CPUs and a shared dispatcher, measuring training/inference FLOPs, MACs, throughput and memory (Table 4), plus convergence against training FLOPs (Figure 7). Section 3.2 newly reports 100-300-iteration updates and a 16-expert vision cap, conflicting with retained per-iteration/8-expert descriptions; these statements do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Tables 6-10 add learning-rate sensitivity evidence across the GLUE configurations. Figure 7 adds compute-based convergence analysis for COLA and MRPC, while Figure 23 adds per-layer distributions of activated-expert counts for three backbones. Earlier loss and test-time top-k ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix A in both versions reports averaging vision and language results over three random seeds. No changed run count, confidence interval, significance test or uncertainty-estimation practice is introduced; new efficiency results are point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark tables retain their scores, including v1 Tables 5-6 as v2 Tables 11-12. New results include learning-rate grids, convergence and routing summaries, and Table 4 resource measurements. For example, DYNMoE/MoE-LLaVA StableLM throughput is 26/19 tokens/s with equal memory. Qwen training cost is slightly higher for DYNMoE: 34.61 versus 34.27 TFLOPs/step.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations are retained, with no added theorem, proof or derivation. Remark 3.1 supplies conceptual motivation for the existing unweighted expert averaging.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the claims of automatic expert configuration, competitive cross-modal performance and efficiency through fewer activated parameters. Adding 'and efficiency' to the contribution bullet reiterates an existing claim.

C2.justification: Remark 3.1 newly explains unweighted averaging through independently calculated expert-score scales. Section 4.3 connects higher BERT expert activation counts with fixed-k performance. The shared-expert interpretation emphasized in Section 4.5 already existed in v1 Appendix C.4.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the GLUE learning-rate grid {2e-5, 3e-5, 5e-5}, best-rate selection and hardware/dispatcher controls for efficiency measurements. The detailed training-configuration table is unchanged from v1 Table 4 to v2 Table 5, as are code-access information and existing training-resource disclosures.

R1.justification: The 57 references and Related Works section are unchanged. The shared-expert connection to DeepSeek-MoE, now emphasized in the main text, was already explicit in v1 Appendix C.4.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized explanatory additions, expands the efficiency discussion, retitles Section 4.5 and updates author/affiliation text. The overall argument, section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds six tables and Figures 7 and 23, revises Figure 4 with activation annotations and a top-two-ranking panel, combines existing plots in Figure 1, and substantially rearranges figure placement. Some Figure 4 score axes are misleadingly relabeled 'Top-1 Accuracy Times'. Existing appendix plots are largely relocated or resized.

improvement.justification: v1 mainly supports efficiency through activated-parameter counts; v2 adds controlled resource measurements and convergence curves, strengthening that evidence. Learning-rate tables also make the retained GLUE comparisons more transparent. These gains are tempered by conflicting expert-cap/update descriptions and misleading Figure 4 labels, yielding a limited overall improvement.
